title: High-norms hypercontractivity for the noise operator
statement:
Fix a natural number $n$. Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $p, u$ be real exponents
with $2 \le p \le u$. Suppose $\rho \in \bbr$ satisfies $0 \le \rho \le 1$ together with
$\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$. Then, with expectations taken under the uniform measure
on $\{0,1\}^n$ and $T_\rho$ the noise operator, the higher $L^u$ norm of the noised
function is bounded by the lower $L^p$ norm of $f$:
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{T_\rho f}^u\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/u} \;\le\;
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^p\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}.
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n bits
replaced:
For $2 \le p \le u$, any $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho \le 1$ and
$\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(u-1)}$, and $f : \mathrm{BoolCube}\,n \to \bbr$,
\[
  \bigl(\E[\abs{T_\rho f}^u]\bigr)^{1/u} \;\le\; \bigl(\E[\abs{f}^p]\bigr)^{1/p}.
\]
